start.text: The ruts go east between the pines, and bend, the way Wenna said they would, and the fog thins round the bend the way it thins round the colliers' clearing.

A hollow, green under the grey, the floor black with old charcoal dust. A cone hut with its sods slipping and nobody's smoke. A cordwood stack gone silver. And a clamp, sunk to a low grey hump, the front of it fallen in.
Wenna walks ahead of you to the clamp and stops with the lantern held out over it, and stands there.
There it is. There it was all along.
I smelled it the whole way round. Three times. It was burning, and I was walking round it.
